pass_condition: write_records/read_* are the minimal API W4-3 (SQL reprojection) and W4-4 (leaderboard, not-ranked, matrix, repos, evidence, snapshot, reproject) need.

findings.statement: Three of W4-4's seven endpoints have no read path: there is no ranked-rows reader, no snapshot summary, and no matrix query; ranked_order_sql returns only (owner, name, rank, tie_group) and is documented as a parity helper.
findings.quoted_line: def ranked_order_sql(conn: sqlite3.Connection, snapshot_id: str) -> List[tuple]:
findings.failure_scenario: W4-4's leaderboard endpoint has to return full 06 section 4 rows in rank order with limit/offset; today it can only get owner/name pairs from ranked_order_sql and then call get_row per repo -- a Python loop over all rows, which is exactly what W4-4's acceptance forbids ('no Python full scans').

observations: Present and sufficient: get_row (repos/{o}/{n}), get_evidence (repos/{o}/{n}/evidence), list_not_ranked (not-ranked with gate_reason/unrated_reason), get_snapshot (the snapshots row).

Missing, named: list_ranked(conn, snapshot_id, limit, offset) returning full rows; snapshot_summary(conn, snapshot_id) with counts of rated/gated/unrated for GET /v1/cvi/snapshot (04 section 7 asks for counts and a detector summary, get_snapshot returns neither); a matrix projection (leverage/friction/quadrant/coverage) for the matrix endpoint.
_ORDER_BY_SQL is private but its docstring tells W4-3 to reuse it across modules; make it public (and add __all__ to cvi/store/__init__.py, which currently exports nothing).

not_checked.statement: W4-3's persona re-projection SQL and W4-4's endpoints are not in this packet; only the reader helpers they build on were checked.
